chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) validated the testimony of women in debts, and there was no man with them.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women alone sufficient for debts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) permitted women's testimony in financial debts even without a accompanying man, challenging the common reliance on Quran 2:282 which mentions two women for one man. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the competency of women as witnesses in specific financial contexts, independent of the male guarantor often cited in other schools of thought.
